Same problem here.

Chrome version 102.0.5005.62 on Windows 10

Facing the same problem.
(Version 102.0.5005.61 (Official Build) (64-bit) on Mac.

I can reproduce this issue on Chrome Canary (v104) but not on v101. Not sure what has changed on Chrome since v102.
@bvaughn can you help investigate?
Probably not any time soon. I'm pretty swamped at the moment.

I found that the unresponsiveness happens after scrolling, and that inspecting the flamegraph container itself and removing `pointer-events: none` from the `<svg>` makes it responsive again. I don't have the bandwidth to do the fix, but from the source I see in the extension, this might get thrown on the container while scrolling, so something is maybe making it think we're still scrolling? Hopefully someone can take this and run with it!

Editing to add that I also tried the version from March 30th via a CRX and it had the same issue in Chrome 102, so not a recent change. As @mondaychen points out, perhaps an interaction with new Chrome?
@jennazee Good catch re: scrolling. I can click around in the component tree to my heart's content, as long as I don't scroll in the component tree panel.

Thanks @jennazee and @Aaron-Ennis. Yes, I think this is related to scrolling. The component panel uses a `<FixedSizeList>` from [react-window](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-window), which sets `pointerEvents` to `none` when scrolling. 
https://github.com/bvaughn/react-window/blob/master/src/createListComponent.js#L365
My guess is that for some reason the `isScrolling` state is no longer correctly set back to `false`

It's quite strange that when I'm testing the inline version of devtools, this issue does not exist. This might be an extension-only issue.
Before we figure this out and release a fix, if you've already upgraded to Chrome v102 or above, as far as I know it would not be easy to downgrade. You can consider use Firefox for now, or use the [standalone DevTools app](https://github.com/facebook/react/tree/main/packages/react-devtools)

body:
Hey everyone! After some investigation, we discovered that this issue is likely due to `requestAnimationFrame` not getting called in the extension. The reason a lot of you were seeing `pointer-events: none` on components is because the library we use for windowing sets pointer events to none when we scroll. We use `requestAnimationFrame` to determine when scrolling is done. Unfortunately, because `requestAnimationFrame` doesn't call its callback function in extensions for some reason, we never set scrolling to be finished, thus causing this issue.

**We believe this is a Chrome bug**, but because it affects React DevTools, we will put up a temporary while it gets resolved. In the meantime, **please either downgrade your Chrome version or use a different browser** until this is fixed. Thanks so much for reporting this issue!

Nice find!
